<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919103_theRebbe_196__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Korach's error stemmed from his lack of self-nullification, which prevented him from grasping the synthesis of opposites in the firmament's separation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that the reason Korach erred and thought that the intent of the dividing firmament was the separation itself,</t>
    <t s="3">is,</t>
    <t s="4">because he did not possess the quality of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="5">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="6">that this which was stated above</t>
    <t s="7">(section 3)</t>
    <t s="8">—that the intent in the lower waters being separated from the upper waters and descending below was so that they would have a yearning and thirst to ascend upward—</t>
    <t s="9">is a connection and inter-inclusion of two opposite attributes.</t>
    <t s="10">For from the perspective of the chassadim</t>
    <t s="11">(the advantage of revelations),</t>
    <t s="12">the superiority is in the upper waters, and there would be no need for the lower waters to be separated from the upper waters and descend below,</t>
    <t s="13">and from the perspective of the gevuros,</t>
    <t s="14">the superiority is in the revelation of the root of the lower waters themselves,</t>
    <t s="15">and there is no need for the lower waters to have a yearning and thirst to depart from their existence and ascend upward.</t>
    <t s="16">And that the intent in the descent of the lower waters below is that they should have a thirst to ascend upward—this is from the aspect of the Tiferes,</t>
    <t s="17">the central line,</t>
    <t s="18">which connects the opposites of Chessed and Gevurah,</t>
    <t s="19">so that the left is included in the right48.</t>
    <t s="20">And since the matter of inter-inclusion is from the aspect of self-nullification49,</t>
    <t s="21">therefore Korach, who lacked self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="22">this concept was not settled within him.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven" is achieved through self-nullification to fulfill the divine will, not for personal spiritual gratification.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that similarly, regarding the service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven,"</t>
    <t s="2">that even though one knows the great superiority of "in all your ways know Him"—</t>
    <t s="3">the knowledge of G‑dliness within worldly matters themselves—</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless, all his engagement in worldly matters will be only as a means for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="5">this is through self-nullification to fulfill the supernal will.</t>
    <t s="6">For since his service is not to quench his own thirst for a revelation of G‑dliness in his soul,</t>
    <t s="7">but rather he is surrendered and given over to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="8">therefore the revelation of knowing G‑dliness</t>
    <t s="9">(also)</t>
    <t s="10">in worldly matters is of no consequence to him,</t>
    <t s="11">and his entire desire is in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="12">the fulfillment of the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="13">[And through this, he will also have the revelation of G‑dliness that is in worldly matters,</t>
    <t s="14">as explained above</t>
    <t s="15">(section 5),</t>
    <t s="16">that through the service of "all your deeds for the sake of Heaven," one attains "in all your ways know Him."]</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The life that is above nature, accessed through self-nullification, enables one to engage in worldly matters for the sake of Heaven without stumbling.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is [the meaning of] "Hashem, our soul in life, and He did not give our foot to stumbling,"</t>
    <t s="2">for when a person engages in Torah and mitzvos, he is in the aspect of "head," and when he engages in worldly matters, he is in the aspect of "foot,"</t>
    <t s="3">and the power for this—that his feet</t>
    <t s="4">(his engagement in worldly matters)</t>
    <t s="5">will not stumble—</t>
    <t s="6">comes from the life in which "He placed our soul,"</t>
    <t s="7">the life that is above nature,</t>
    <t s="8">which is above the life of the soul itself,</t>
    <t s="9">even from the aspect of "chai be'etzem" (intrinsic life),</t>
    <t s="10">for from the level of the life of the soul itself</t>
    <t s="11">(including also the aspect of "chai be'etzem"),</t>
    <t s="12">it is possible that one will desire the revelation of G‑dliness within worldly matters,</t>
    <t s="13">and when his engagement in worldly matters is for the sake of</t>
    <t s="14">(the revelation within)</t>
    <t s="15">the worldly matters themselves,</t>
    <t s="16">and not for the sake of Heaven for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="17">then his feet</t>
    <t s="18">(his involvement in matters of permission)</t>
    <t s="19">will stumble.</t>
    <t s="20">And in order that his feet not stumble,</t>
    <t s="21">so that his engagement in matters of permission is for the sake of Heaven as above,</t>
    <t s="22">this is through the life that is above nature</t>
    <t s="23">(and it may be said that the vessel for this is self-nullification),</t>
    <t s="24">for being above limitation, they connect the two opposites of Chessed and Gevurah,</t>
    <t s="25">so that even though one knows the superiority in the refinement of matters of permission,</t>
    <t s="26">nevertheless, his intent in doing matters of permission is for the sake of fulfilling Torah and mitzvos.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
